newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: EMU-drive steers Irish central bank policy.
newsitem.headline: EMU-drive steers Irish central bank policy.

text.p: Irish inflation is defying conventional wisdom by falling despite a booming economy. That would give any other European central bank something to cheer about and a chance to trim interest rates in celebration.

Ignoring exporters and farmers' clamour for a rate cut, the central bank indicated in a policy statement on Tuesday that the only party it wants to attend is the one to celebrate Ireland's economic and monetary union (EMU) membership.
Against a background of four-year low inflation, the central bank's statement spotlights the path the central bank is determined to keep on towards its EMU goal in 1999.

Though the Irish pound is bouncing against the ceiling of the ERM grid, Ireland's central bank appears solely concerned with maintaining low inflation so as not to tarnish its EMU membership criteria.
"The exporters are calling for a cut in rates, but the central bank says it is more likely to raise rates if anything threatens inflation," Riada economist Padhraic Garvey said.
"Their main objective is that we meet the inflation criteria for EMU and to keep inflation low," he added.
On Wednesday, disgruntled exporters and farmers again demanded an interest rate cut to curb the rise in the Irish pound, which is now about 11 percent above the weakest currency, the French franc.
Exporters argue the rising Irish pound is threatening multinational subsidiaries across the country and say thousands of jobs will be lost if the punt's appreciation is not reversed.
Ireland's January consumer price index (CPI), the first monthly CPI index to be published, showed a 0.5-percent drop on November 1996 and rose 0.9 percent in the 11 months since February last year.
While the low inflation number would appear to give scope for an interest rate reduction, the central bank seems more concerned with EMU and maintaining price stability.

"Domestic monetary policy from now to the time of decision on the membership of EMU must be conducted in such a manner as to ensure that the price stability criterion for joining the Union is satisfied and that the scene is set for successful membership on an ongoing basis," the central bank said in Tuesday's monetary statement.
